quarterly_data.quarter: Sakura Internet annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (annual securities report): net sales JPY 35,301,649 thousand (+12.4%), a record, as the focus areas GPU infrastructure services and cloud services grew and large government orders contributed to other services; operating loss JPY 403,654 thousand (prior year: operating profit JPY 4,145,586 thousand) on personnel investment for cloud-service feature development and sales promotion, higher depreciation from GPU-related investment, server maintenance, data-center rent and cost of services for other-services sales; ordinary profit JPY 105,477 thousand (-97.4%), supported by subsidy income under the Cloud Program; profit attributable to owners of parent JPY 216,023 thousand (-92.6%)
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 net sales JPY 35,301,649 thousand (+12.4%); operating loss JPY 403,654 thousand

quarterly_data.quarter: Sakura Internet annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 sales by service category (the "GPU cloud services" category was renamed "GPU infrastructure services" and categories were partly reclassified; year-on-year on the restated basis): cloud services JPY 15,324,068 thousand (+9.4%) on SAKURA Cloud and SAKURA Rental Server; GPU infrastructure services JPY 8,144,342 thousand (+20.3%) after the bare-metal GPU cloud service Koukaryoku PHY launched an H200 plan and a B200 service using NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs; physical base services JPY 3,056,750 thousand (-7.2%) on lower housing and dedicated-server usage; other services JPY 8,776,488 thousand (+19.6%) on large government projects. GPU infrastructure services comprise bare-metal Koukaryoku PHY and SAKURA ONE, a managed HPC cluster service the company built itself for large language model development; the VM-type GPU cloud Koukaryoku VRT is reported in cloud services
quarterly_data.figure: GPU infrastructure services JPY 8,144,342 thousand (+20.3%); cloud services JPY 15,324,068 thousand (+9.4%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Sakura Internet annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management targets (annual securities report): sustained year-on-year net sales growth of 10% or more, gross margin of 30% or more and ordinary profit margin of 10% or more. In FY2026 the sales target was met with record revenue, but gross margin of 22.5% (prior year 35.8%) and ordinary profit margin of 0.3% (prior year 12.9%) fell below target because of active investment in people, GPUs and container-type data centers for medium- to long-term growth and higher cost of services for other-services sales, which management calls a temporary burden that contributes to medium- to long-term value. For the fiscal year ending March 2027 the company expects sales growth from GPU infrastructure services and cloud services; investment in next-generation GPU resources and data centers will continue as planned, but the year gives top priority to stable operation of existing GPU resources, with additional investment to be considered in light of market trends
quarterly_data.figure: targets: sales growth 10%+, gross margin 30%+, ordinary profit margin 10%+; FY2026 gross margin 22.5%, ordinary margin 0.3%

quarterly_data.quarter: Sakura Internet annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management states that investment following METI's certification of its Cloud Program supply-assurance plan has advanced the securing of GPU resources and the build-out of data-center infrastructure, and the company is becoming established as a core player in generative-AI infrastructure, and that it will use its official selection for the Government Cloud to expand public-sector and enterprise sales channels through partner collaboration and strategic alliances; it cites rising expectations for domestic public cloud from an economic-security standpoint and growing demand for GPUs and other advanced compute driven by generative AI

quarterly_data.quarter: Sakura Internet annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: New-facility plans at Ishikari Data Center as of March 31, 2026: the next GPU investment (GPU, network and storage equipment) is to start June 2026 or later, with the GPUs, amount and timing still under consideration, so its planned amount and completion are undetermined; the container-type data center (JPY 17,000 million total, JPY 7,965 million paid, started June 2024) has no set completion date because the next and later GPU investments are not decided; Building 3 zones C and D and the Building 2 generator (JPY 5,300 million, JPY 663 million paid, started March 2025) are planned for completion in April 2027
